channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Senate Democrat Chris Murphy Hospitalized Due to a Stroke
item.description: Senate Democrat Chris Murphy was hospitalized after suffering a stroke Saturday afternoon, his office disclosed on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Canada, US to Outline Trade Plan in Weeks Ahead, Carney Says
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he spoke with President Donald Trump and both sides would work on a “mutually beneficial” US-Canadian trade deal in the weeks ahead.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Hughes

item.title: Presidential Win Strengthens Bulgaria’s Ukraine-Skeptic Leader
item.description: Bulgaria’s incumbent President Iliana Yotova won the presidential election on Sunday, helping to cement Ukraine-skeptic Prime Minister Rumen Radev’s grip on power in the euro-area country.
item.dc:creator: Slav Okov

item.title: DOJ Lawsuit to Probe Alaska Senate Vote Thrown Out by Judge
item.description: A federal judge dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit that sought to preemptively stop Alaska election officials from certifying the results of the state’s US Senate contest if the Republican candidate loses by a small margin.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg, Matthew Griffin and María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Feud Erupts in Michigan as El-Sayed Rival Backs GOP’s Rogers
item.description: Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary for Michigan’s US Senate seat, backed Republican candidate Mike Rogers, breaking with Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed and exacerbating a split between progressives and moderate party members.
item.dc:creator: David Welch and María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Gulf States Fear Fiercer Iran Retaliation If US Strikes Again
item.description: Gulf states fear that another US-Israeli attack on a better-prepared Iran could unleash an even more destructive war across the region, leaving them to pick up the pieces.
item.dc:creator: Peter Martin

item.title: Midterm Results Could Reshape Both Parties
item.description: Hosts of Bloomberg's Balance of Power Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu join Bloomberg This Weekend and discuss that President Donald Trump is making a late campaign push in traditionally Republican states as the midterm elections test his influence over voters and the Republican Party. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, they examine how the results could reshape both parties, the importance of closely watched races from Texas to Michigan and the possibility that control of Congress may not be known immediately. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He May Be ‘Mr. Veto’ If Democrats Win Midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump said he may have to become “Mr. Veto” if Democrats win a majority in Tuesday’s midterms, according to a clip of a New York Post interview aired Sunday on Fox News.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim and María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Why Socialism Is Back in American Politics
item.description: Socialism was once widely seen as politically disqualifying in the United States, but democratic socialist candidates and ideas are gaining greater visibility, particularly among younger voters. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan and investor Steven Rattner argue that frustration over affordability, inequality and economic insecurity is making voters more receptive to alternatives to traditional free-market policies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India Protest Renew Calls for Election Chief Resignation
item.description: India’s opposition parties on Sunday renewed calls for the resignation of the country’s election chief, staging fresh protests in the latest display of public dissent against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. DeLauro Sees Cost of Living Fueling Democratic Gains
item.description: Rep. Rosa DeLauro of Connecticut tells Bloomberg This Weekend she expects a Democratic wave in the midterm elections, arguing that concerns over affordability and the cost of living are driving voters toward her party. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, DeLauro says that if Democrats win the House and she reclaims the Appropriations Committee gavel, she would focus on affordability, oversight and accountability rather than impeachment. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Says Teen Held After US Warning on Moscow Terror Threat
item.description: Russia’s Federal Security Service said it detained a minor teenaged boy on suspicion of planning a terrorist attack on a Moscow park and museum, a day after a warning from US officials.
item.dc:creator: Tony Halpin

item.title: Riot and Looting Erupts Overnight in Frankfurt
item.description: On Saturday night, police remained on duty in downtown Frankfurt after riots broke out following a demonstration on Saturday. Storefronts were smashed, shops looted, and police officers attacked. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Agrees to Halt Recruitment of Ghanaians for Ukraine War
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to halt the recruitment of Ghanaians to fight in Ukraine after President John Mahama raised concerns about the practice, according to Ghana’s foreign minister.
item.dc:creator: Moses Mozart Dzawu

item.title: Iran’s Long Game Complicates Trump’s War Plans
item.description: Bloomberg White House National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Iran’s strategy of prolonging its conflict with the US is testing President Donald Trump’s desire for a faster resolution, with the midterm elections adding political pressure to his decisions. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Jamrisko says Iran views regime survival as a victory, while economic pressure, regional instability and the risk of a failed state complicate the path forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Banks on Rallies to Turn Out MAGA Faithful One More Time
item.description: Donald Trump is capping his final electoral campaign the way he began over a decade ago: hoping a whirlwind sprint across the country will turn out his most fervent supporters and thwart Democratic designs to curtail his power in the sunset of his political career.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse, Mario Parker, Catherine Lucey and Erik Wasson

item.title: Democrats Eye House and Senate Gains
item.description: Rutgers University polling director Ashley Koning and Bloomberg Opinion Senior Executive Editor Tim O’Brien tell Bloomberg This Weekend that Democrats enter the midterm elections with momentum as concerns about affordability and President Donald Trump’s approval weigh on Republicans. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, they examine the possibility of Democratic gains in the House and Senate, the reliability of polling and what a Republican defeat could mean for Trump’s influence over the party. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 2026 Midterm Elections: What a Democratic Win Would Mean for Trump
item.description: In his second term, President Donald Trump so far has benefited from his Republican Party holding majorities in both houses of Congress, as he did in the top half of his first turn in the White House. When one party controls both the presidency and Congress, ambitious legislation can become law, as evidenced by the tax-cut measures enacted under Trump in 2017 and 2025. And with party faithful running congressional committees, a presidential administration is insulated, to some extent, from tough
item.dc:creator: Greg Giroux

item.title: AI Concerns Move to Center of Midterm Campaigns
item.description: Bloomberg Government senior AI and government reporter Cristiano Lima-Strong tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI is emerging as a major issue in the midterm elections, as candidates clash over regulation, data centers, jobs and safety. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Lima-Strong explains that Democratic control of Congress could bring a more aggressive regulatory approach as lawmakers debate how to balance safeguards with innovation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India’s Protest Movements Unite in Fresh Headache for Modi
item.description: Protesters began gathering in New Delhi for a major opposition rally over voter rolls that has drawn increasingly sharp criticism from India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia and Atul Dev
